        redisHostname = url.hostname;
        useTLS = url.protocol === 'rediss:'; // only TLS if scheme says so
      } catch (e) {
        logger.error('Failed to parse REDIS_URL', { error: e.message });
      }
    }
    
    const redisOptions = {
      maxRetriesPerRequest: null, // Required for BullMQ
      enableReadyCheck: false,
    
      // ✅ FIX: TLS configuration based on protocol
      ...(useTLS && {
        tls: {
          servername: redisHostname || undefined,
          rejectUnauthorized: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
        },
      }),
    
      retryStrategy(times) {
        const delay = Math.min(times * 100, 3000);
        return delay;
      },
    };
    
    let redis;
    
    function getRedis() {
      if (!redis) {
        // Check if REDIS_URL exists
        if (!process.env.REDIS_URL) {
          logger.error('REDIS_URL environment variable is not set');
          throw new Error('REDIS_URL is required');
        }
    
        logger.info('Connecting to Redis', {
          host: redisHostname,
          tlsEnabled: useTLS
        });
    
        redis = new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL, redisOptions);
    
        redis.on('error', (err) => {
          logger.error('Redis error', { error: err.message, stack: err.stack });
        });
    
        redis.on('connect', () => {
          logger.info('Redis connected successfully');
        });
    
        redis.on('ready', () => {
          logger.info('Redis ready');
        });
    
        redis.on('close', () => {
          logger.warn('Redis connection closed');
        });
    
        redis.on('reconnecting', () => {
          logger.warn('Redis reconnecting...');
        });
      }
      return redis;
    }
    
    async function checkConnection() {
      try {
        const r = getRedis();
        await r.ping();
        return true;
      } catch (error) {
        logger.error('Redis connection check failed', { error: error.message });
        return false;
      }
    }
    
    // Graceful shutdown
    async function disconnectRedis() {
      if (redis) {
        try {
          await redis.quit();
          logger.info('Redis disconnected gracefully');
        } catch (error) {
          logger.error('Error disconnecting Redis', { error: error.message });
        }
      }
    }
    
    module.exports = { getRedis, checkConnection, disconnectRedis };
    // src/server.js
    require('dotenv').config();
    
    // ── Environment validation ─────────────────────────────────────────
    // Fail fast with a clear message if required variables are missing.
    function validateEnvironment() {
      const required = [
        'SUPABASE_URL',
        'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY',
        'REDIS_URL',
        'FRONTEND_URL',
      ];
    
      const missing = required.filter((key) => !process.env[key]);
    
      if (missing.length > 0) {
        // Use process.stderr directly — logger may depend on env vars itself
        process.stderr.write(
          `[FATAL] Missing required environment variables: ${missing.join(', ')}\n` +
          `        Set these in your .env file before starting the server.\n`
        );
        process.exit(1);
      }
    }
    
    validateEnvironment();
    
    // Sentry must be initialised before anything else
    if (process.env.SENTRY_DSN) {
      const Sentry = require('@sentry/node');
      Sentry.init({
        dsn:              process.env.SENTRY_DSN,
        environment:      process.env.NODE_ENV || 'development',
        tracesSampleRate: 0.1,
      });
    }
    
    const app    = require('./app');
    const logger = require('./utils/logger');
    const { checkConnection: checkDb }    = require('./config/database');
    const { checkConnection: checkRedis } = require('./config/redis');
    
    const PORT = parseInt(process.env.PORT) || 3000;
    
    async function start() {
      logger.info('Running pre-flight checks...');
    
      try {
        const dbOk = await checkDb();
        if (!dbOk) throw new Error('Database connection failed');
        logger.info('✓ Database connected');
    
        const redisOk = await checkRedis();
        if (!redisOk) logger.warn('⚠ Redis not connected — queues disabled');
        else logger.info('✓ Redis connected');
      } catch (err) {
        logger.error('Pre-flight check failed', { error: err.message });
        process.exit(1);
      }
    
      const server = app.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {
        logger.info('Kith API running', {
          port: PORT,
          env:  process.env.NODE_ENV,
          url:  process.env.API_BASE_URL || `http://localhost:${PORT}`,
        });
      });
    
      // Explicit timeouts instead of relying on Node defaults. keepAliveTimeout
      // must stay LOWER than any upstream load balancer's own idle timeout
      // (e.g. ALB defaults to 60s) to avoid a race where the LB reuses a
      // connection Node has already started closing. headersTimeout must be
      // greater than keepAliveTimeout per Node's own requirement.
      server.keepAliveTimeout = 65 * 1000;
      server.headersTimeout   = 66 * 1000;
    
      // Graceful shutdown
      const shutdown = (signal) => {
        logger.info(`${signal} received — shutting down gracefully`);
        server.close(() => {
          logger.info('HTTP server closed');
          process.exit(0);
        });
    
        // Force exit after 10 s if connections hang
        setTimeout(() => {
          logger.error('Forced exit after timeout');
          process.exit(1);
        }, 10000);
      };
    
      process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown('SIGTERM'));
      process.on('SIGINT',  () => shutdown('SIGINT'));
    
      process.on('unhandledRejection', (reason) => {
        logger.error('Unhandled promise rejection', { reason: String(reason) });
      });
    
      process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => {
        logger.error('Uncaught exception', { error: err.message, stack: err.stack });
        process.exit(1);
      });
    }
    
    start();

          workspaceId: req.query.workspace_id,

    }

    }

      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }

    // src/utils/response.js
    
    function success(res, data, statusCode = 200, meta = null) {
      const body = { data };
      if (meta) body.meta = meta;
      return res.status(statusCode).json(body);
    }
    
    function paginate(res, data, total, page, perPage) {
      return success(res, data, 200, {
        pagination: {
          page: parseInt(page),
          per_page: parseInt(perPage),
          total,
          total_pages: Math.ceil(total / perPage),
        },
      });
    }
    
    function noContent(res) {

    }

    const { AppError } = require('../utils/errors');
    const { ZodError }  = require('zod');
    const logger        = require('../utils/logger');
    
    function errorHandler(err, req, res, next) {
      // Zod validation errors
      if (err instanceof ZodError) {
        const firstError = err.errors[0];
        return res.status(400).json({
          error: {
            code:    'VALIDATION_FAILED',
            message: firstError.message,
            field:   firstError.path.join('.'),
            details: err.errors.map((e) => ({
              field:   e.path.join('.'),
              message: e.message,
              code:    e.code,
            })),
          },
        });
      }
    
      // Known application errors
      if (err instanceof AppError) {
        const body = {
          error: {
            code:    err.code,
            message: err.message,
          },
        };
        if (err.field)   body.error.field   = err.field;
        if (err.details) body.error.details = err.details;
    
        if (err.statusCode >= 500) {
          logger.error('Application error', {
            request_id: req.requestId,
            code:       err.code,
            message:    err.message,
            stack:      err.stack,
          });
        }
    
        return res.status(err.statusCode).json(body);
      }
    
      // Postgres unique-violation
      if (err.code === '23505') {
        return res.status(409).json({
          error: { code: 'CONFLICT', message: 'A record with this data already exists.' },
        });
      }
    
      // Postgres foreign-key violation
      if (err.code === '23503') {
        return res.status(422).json({
          error: { code: 'BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION', message: 'Referenced resource does not exist.' },
        });
      }
    
      // Unhandled / unexpected errors
      logger.error('Unhandled error', {
        request_id: req.requestId,
        message:    err.message,
        stack:      err.stack,
      });
    
      const message =
        process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'An internal error occurred' : err.message;
    
      return res.status(500).json({
        error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message },
      });
    }
    
    module.exports = { errorHandler };

    // tests/mocks/supabase.mock.js
    //
    // The single most important shared test utility in this project (see
    // Doc 4 Section 2.5's header note). Given how many service functions
    // make 3–6 SEQUENTIAL Supabase calls (list-then-detail, fetch-then-
    // update, parallel Promise.all fan-outs), every service unit test needs
    // to script "call 1 returns X, call 2 returns Y, call 3 errors" without
    // hand-rolling that sequencing per test file.
    //
    // USAGE
    // -----
    //   const { mockSupabase } = require('../../mocks/supabase.mock');
    //
    //   jest.mock('../../../src/config/supabase', () => {
    //     const { mockSupabase } = require('../../mocks/supabase.mock');
    //     const instance = mockSupabase();
    //     global.__supabaseMock = instance; // expose for the test file to script
    //     return { supabaseAdmin: instance.client, supabase: instance.client, supabaseAuth: instance.client };
    //   });
    //
    //   // in a test:
    //   const { mockNextResponse } = global.__supabaseMock;
    //   mockNextResponse({ data: { id: 'abc' }, error: null });      // response to call #1
    //   mockNextResponse({ data: [{ id: 'x' }], error: null, count: 1 }); // response to call #2
    //   const result = await someService.doThing({ ... });
    //
    // Prefer the exported `createSupabaseMock()` helper below (used by
    // tests/mocks/index.js and every service unit test in this package) over
    // constructing this by hand — it wires the jest.mock() call for you.
    //
    // DESIGN NOTES
    // ------------
    // - Every query-builder method returns `builder` (chainable), matching
    //   supabase-js's own fluent API.
    // - `.single()` / `.maybeSingle()` and awaiting the builder directly
    //   (`await query`, via `.then`) all pull from the SAME sequential
    //   `responses` queue, advanced by a single shared `callIndex`. This
    //   matches how supabase-js queries actually resolve — a query is a
    //   thenable, and `.single()`/`.maybeSingle()` are just the terminal
    //   call that makes it await-able with a different unwrap shape — so
    //   scripting responses in the order your service code issues queries
    //   is the correct mental model regardless of which terminal method it
    //   uses.
    // - `.rpc()` is tracked SEPARATELY from the main response queue (its own
    //   `rpcResponses` queue) since RPC calls don't go through
    //   `.from()`/`.select()` chaining at all in supabase-js — they're a
    //   distinct top-level method on the client. Script RPC responses with
    //   `mockNextRpcResponse()`.
    // - `.storage.from(bucket)` is also modeled separately (see
    //   `storageBuilder`) since storage.service.js calls
    //   `supabase.storage.from(BUCKET).createSignedUploadUrl(...)` /
    //   `.download(...)` / `.remove(...)` / `.createSignedUrl(...)`, a
    //   completely different chain shape from the Postgres query builder.
    // - `.auth` methods used directly on the client (auth.getUser,
    //   auth.admin.signOut, auth.admin.updateUserById,
    //   auth.admin.getUserById, auth.signInWithPassword, auth.signUp, etc.)
    //   are separately mockable jest.fn()s on `client.auth` / `client.auth.admin`
    //   — script them directly, e.g. `client.auth.getUser.mockResolvedValue(...)`.
    
    function createChainableBuilder(state) {
      const builder = {};
    
      const chainMethods = [
        'from', 'select', 'insert', 'update', 'delete', 'upsert',
        'eq', 'neq', 'in', 'is', 'not', 'gte', 'lte', 'lt', 'gt',
        'order', 'range', 'limit', 'ilike', 'like', 'or', 'filter',
        'contains', 'textSearch',
      ];
    
      for (const method of chainMethods) {
        builder[method] = jest.fn((...args) => {
          // `.delete({ count: 'exact' })` and similar option-passing calls
          // are recorded but otherwise behave like any other chain link.
          state.calls.push({ method, args });
          return builder;
        });
      }
    
      function nextResponse() {
        const resp = state.responses[state.callIndex] ?? { data: null, error: null, count: 0 };
        state.callIndex += 1;
        return resp;
      }
    
      builder.single = jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(nextResponse()));
      builder.maybeSingle = jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(nextResponse()));

      // directly (no terminal .single()/.maybeSingle()/.then() call needed),
      // exactly like a real supabase-js PostgrestFilterBuilder, which is a
      // thenable.
      builder.then = (resolve, reject) => {
        return Promise.resolve(nextResponse()).then(resolve, reject);
      };
      builder.catch = (reject) => builder.then(undefined, reject);
    
      return builder;
    }

          createSignedUploadUrl: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(state.storageResponses[state.storageCallIndex++] ?? { data: { signedUrl: 'https://storage.test/signed-upload' }, error: null })),
          createSignedUrl:       jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(state.storageResponses[state.storageCallIndex++] ?? { data: { signedUrl: 'https://storage.test/signed-download' }, error: null })),
          download:               jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(state.storageResponses[state.storageCallIndex++] ?? { data: { arrayBuffer: () => Promise.resolve(new ArrayBuffer(0)) }, error: null })),
          remove:                 jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(state.storageResponses[state.storageCallIndex++] ?? { data: [{}], error: null })),
        })),
      };
    }

          state.rpcCalls.push({ fnName, params });
          const resp = state.rpcResponses[state.rpcCallIndex] ?? { data: null, error: null };
          state.rpcCallIndex += 1;
          return Promise.resolve(resp);
        }),
        storage,
        auth: {
          getUser: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: { user: null }, error: null })),
          signInWithPassword: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: {}, error: null })),
          signUp: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: {}, error: null })),
          refreshSession: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: {}, error: null })),
          resetPasswordForEmail: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: {}, error: null })),
          verifyOtp: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: {}, error: null })),
          exchangeCodeForSession: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ data: {}, error: null })),

        mockNextResponse: (resp) => state.responses.push(resp),

        mockNextRpcResponse: (resp) => state.rpcResponses.push(resp),
    
        /** Push the response for the NEXT .storage.from(...).<method>() call. */
        mockNextStorageResponse: (resp) => state.storageResponses.push(resp),

        reset: () => {
          state.calls = [];
          state.responses = [];
          state.callIndex = 0;
          state.rpcCalls = [];
          state.rpcResponses = [];
          state.rpcCallIndex = 0;
          state.storageResponses = [];
          state.storageCallIndex = 0;
          jest.clearAllMocks();
        },
      };
    }

    // src/services/membership-cache.service.js
    //
    // Short-lived (30s) Redis cache for requireMembership's per-request
    // lookup of { member, workspace }. requireMembership runs on every
    // single route in workspace.routes.js — dozens of endpoints — so this
    // removes two DB round trips (workspace_members + workspaces) from the
    // hot path for the large majority of requests, which arrive in bursts
    // from the same user within a short window (e.g. a dashboard screen
    // firing several sub-requests).
    //
    // SECURITY TRADEOFF (explicit, by design): authorization-relevant fields
    // — role, is_active — are part of the cached payload. A change made
    // through updateMember/deleteMember/deleteWorkspace is invalidated
    // immediately via invalidateMembership()/invalidateWorkspace() below, so
    // the only residual staleness window is for state changes made OUTSIDE
    // this application (e.g. a direct DB edit) or any future write path that
    // forgets to call invalidate — bounded to a maximum of
    // TTL.MEMBERSHIP_CACHE_SECONDS (30s) either way.
    //
    // Fails open on Redis errors: a cache miss/error just means "fetch from
    // Postgres like before," never a wrongly-granted or wrongly-denied
    // request.
    
    const { getRedis } = require('../config/redis');
    const { TTL, membershipKey } = require('../config/redis-keys');
    const logger = require('../utils/logger');
    
    async function getCachedMembership(workspaceId, userId) {
      try {
        const redis = getRedis();
        const raw = await redis.get(membershipKey(workspaceId, userId));
        if (!raw) return null;
        return JSON.parse(raw);
      } catch (err) {
        logger.warn('Membership cache read failed — falling back to DB', { workspaceId, userId, error: err.message });
        return null;
      }
    }
    
    async function setCachedMembership(workspaceId, userId, payload) {
      try {
        const redis = getRedis();
        await redis.set(
          membershipKey(workspaceId, userId),
          JSON.stringify(payload),
          'EX',
          TTL.MEMBERSHIP_CACHE_SECONDS
        );
      } catch (err) {
        logger.warn('Membership cache write failed', { workspaceId, userId, error: err.message });
      }
    }
    
    /** Invalidate one user's cached membership in one workspace. */
    async function invalidateMembership(workspaceId, userId) {
      if (!workspaceId || !userId) return;
      try {
        const redis = getRedis();
        await redis.del(membershipKey(workspaceId, userId));
      } catch (err) {
        logger.warn('Membership cache invalidation failed', { workspaceId, userId, error: err.message });
      }
    }
    
    /**
     * Invalidate every cached membership for a workspace (e.g. on workspace
     * deletion). Uses SCAN rather than KEYS to avoid blocking Redis on large
     * keyspaces.
     */
    async function invalidateWorkspace(workspaceId) {
      try {
        const redis = getRedis();
        const pattern = membershipKey(workspaceId, '*');
        let cursor = '0';
        do {
          const [nextCursor, keys] = await redis.scan(cursor, 'MATCH', pattern, 'COUNT', 100);
          cursor = nextCursor;
          if (keys.length) await redis.del(...keys);
        } while (cursor !== '0');
      } catch (err) {
        logger.warn('Workspace-wide membership cache invalidation failed', { workspaceId, error: err.message });
      }
    }
    
    module.exports = {
      getCachedMembership,
      setCachedMembership,
      invalidateMembership,
      invalidateWorkspace,
    };

    //
    // This mocks getRedis() to return a shared ioredis-mock instance for the

    // NOTE: ioredis-mock supports the SET...NX EX pattern used by

    //
    // CRUD/settings/announce/avatar logic lives in services/workspace.service.js.
    // This file parses requests, applies validation schemas, calls the

    const { success } = require('../utils/response');
    const { uploadFileSchema }  = require('../validators/ledger.validator');
    const {
      createWorkspaceSchema,
      updateWorkspaceSchema,
      updateSettingsSchema,
      announceSchema,
    } = require('../validators/workspace.validator');
    const audit = require('../services/audit.service');
    const workspaceService = require('../services/workspace.service');
    
    async function listWorkspaces(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const memberships = await workspaceService.listWorkspacesForUser({ userId: req.user.id });
        success(res, { memberships });
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function createWorkspace(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const data = createWorkspaceSchema.parse(req.body);
        const result = await workspaceService.createWorkspace({ userId: req.user.id, ...data });
        success(res, result, 201);
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function getWorkspace(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        const workspace = await workspaceService.getWorkspaceById({ workspaceId });
        success(res, { workspace, current_member: req.member });
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function getAvatarUploadUrl(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const data = uploadFileSchema.parse(req.body);
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        const result = await workspaceService.generateWorkspaceAvatarUploadUrl({
          workspaceId,
          filename:    data.filename,
          contentType: data.content_type,
          fileSize:    data.file_size,
        });
        success(res, result);
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function updateWorkspace(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const data = updateWorkspaceSchema.parse(req.body);
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        const workspace = await workspaceService.updateWorkspace({ workspaceId, data, actorCtx: audit.fromReq(req) });
        success(res, { workspace });
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function deleteWorkspace(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        await workspaceService.deleteWorkspace({ workspaceId, actorCtx: audit.fromReq(req) });
        success(res, { message: 'Workspace deleted.' });
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function getSettings(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        const settings = await workspaceService.getSettings({ workspaceId });
        success(res, { settings });
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function updateSettings(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const data = updateSettingsSchema.parse(req.body);
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        const settings = await workspaceService.updateSettings({
          workspaceId,
          data,
          actorMemberId: req.member.id,
          actorCtx: audit.fromReq(req),
        });
        success(res, { settings });
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    async function announceToWorkspace(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const { workspaceId } = req.params;
        const { title, body, target_role } = announceSchema.parse(req.body);
        const result = await workspaceService.announceToWorkspace({
          workspaceId, title, body, target_role, actorCtx: audit.fromReq(req),
        });
        success(res, result);
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }

    const { getMyContext, getDashboard, getOverdueSummary } = require('./read-tools.service');
    const { findMember, findContainer } = require('./resolution-tools.service');
    const { entitySearchSchema } = require('../../validators/search.validator');
    
    const tools = Object.freeze([
      Object.freeze({
        name: 'get_my_context',
        description: 'Get your identity, role, and current workspace.',
        parameterSchema: z.object({}).strict(),
        minRole: 'member',
        tier: 0,
        handler: getMyContext,
      }),
      Object.freeze({
        name: 'find_member',
        description: 'Find ranked member candidates by name in your workspace. Ask the user to choose among ambiguous matches or confirm a single match before using it in a write. If has_more is true, narrow the query or increase the limit.',
        parameterSchema: entitySearchSchema,
        minRole: 'member',
        tier: 0,
        handler: findMember,
      }),
      Object.freeze({
        name: 'find_container',
        description: 'Find ranked container candidates by name in your workspace. Ask the user to choose among ambiguous matches or confirm a single match before using it in a write. If has_more is true, narrow the query or increase the limit.',
        parameterSchema: entitySearchSchema,
        minRole: 'member',
        tier: 0,
        handler: findContainer,
      }),
      Object.freeze({
        name: 'get_dashboard',
        description: 'Get the current workspace dashboard with your permitted view and personal task summary.',
        parameterSchema: z.object({}).strict(),
        minRole: 'member',
        tier: 1,
        handler: getDashboard,
      }),
      Object.freeze({
        name: 'get_overdue_summary',
        description: 'Get the workspace overdue contribution summary. Admin access required.',
        parameterSchema: z.object({}).strict(),
        minRole: 'admin',
        tier: 1,
        handler: getOverdueSummary,
      }),
    ]);
    
    /** Return role-filtered definitions; executable handlers stay private. */
    function getAvailableTools(context) {
      assertAgentContext(context);
      return Object.freeze(tools
        .filter((tool) => tool.minRole === 'member' || context.member.role === 'admin')
        .map(({ handler, ...definition }) => Object.freeze(definition)));
    }
    
    /**
     * Execute validated reads only. A future proposal executor must be a
     * separate entry point; no model-controlled flag can enable writes here.
     * Results remain service data, including any untrusted user-generated text.
     */
    async function executeReadTool({ name, args = {}, context, turnId }) {
      const startedAt = Date.now();
      const tool = tools.find((candidate) => candidate.name === name);
      const trace = {
        turnId,
        toolName: typeof name === 'string' ? name : null,
        tier: tool?.tier,
        workspaceId: context?.workspace?.id,
        actorUserId: context?.userId,
        actorMemberId: context?.member?.id,
      };
    
      try {
        assertAgentContext(context);
        if (!tool) throw new NotFoundError('Agent tool not found');
        assertAgentContext(context, tool.minRole);
        if (tool.tier > 1) {
          throw new BusinessRuleError('Write tools require an approved proposal');
        }
    
        const parsed = tool.parameterSchema.safeParse(args);
        if (!parsed.success) {
          throw new ValidationError('Invalid tool arguments', null, parsed.error.issues);
        }
    
        trace.parameters = parsed.data;
        const result = await tool.handler({ context, args: parsed.data });
        logger.info('Agent read tool completed', {
          ...trace, result, durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt, outcome: 'success',
        });
        return result;
      } catch (err) {
        logger.warn('Agent read tool failed', {
          ...trace,
          error: err.message,
          errorCode: err.code,
          durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
          outcome: 'error',
        });
        throw err;
      }
    }
    
    module.exports = { getAvailableTools, executeReadTool };
    const { z } = require('zod');
    
    const READ_TURN_LIMITS = Object.freeze({
      modelCalls: 6,
      toolCalls: 12, // Includes the initial get_my_context read.
      messageChars: 8000,
      replyChars: 16000,
      argumentChars: 8000,
      toolResultBytes: 64 * 1024,
      conversationBytes: 128 * 1024,
    });
    
    // Only text comes from the client. Context and provider are server-owned.
    const readTurnInputSchema = z.object({
      message: z.string().max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.messageChars).trim().min(1),
    }).strict();
    
    const providerToolCallSchema = z.object({
      id: z.string().min(1).max(128).regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/),
      name: z.string().min(1).max(64).regex(/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/),
      arguments: z.string().max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.argumentChars),
    }).strict();
    
    // The provider adapter normalizes its response into this contract.
    const readProviderReplySchema = z.object({
      text: z.string().max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.replyChars).nullable().default(null),
      toolCalls: z.array(providerToolCallSchema).max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolCalls).default([]),
    }).strict().refine((reply) => reply.toolCalls.length > 0 || Boolean(reply.text?.trim()), {
      message: 'A provider reply must contain text or tool calls',
    });
    
    module.exports = { READ_TURN_LIMITS, readTurnInputSchema, readProviderReplySchema, providerToolCallSchema };

    // src/queues/index.js
    //
    // Central BullMQ queue registry.
    // Queues are created lazily on first access and cached so the same
    // Queue instance is reused across the process lifetime.
    
    const { Queue } = require('bullmq');
    const { getRedis } = require('../config/redis');
    
    const QUEUE_NAMES = [
      'notification-queue',
      'reminder-queue',
      'cycle-generation-queue',
      'cycle-lifecycle-queue',
      'task-overdue-queue',
      'invite-cleanup-queue',
      'engagement-check-queue',
      'notification-outbox-queue',
      'data-export-queue',
    ];
    
    /** @type {Map<string, import('bullmq').Queue>} */
    const queues = new Map();
    
    /**
     * Returns a shared Queue instance for the given name.
     * Throws if the name is not in QUEUE_NAMES to prevent typo-based
     * queue proliferation.
     *
     * @param {string} name
     * @returns {import('bullmq').Queue}
     */
    function getQueue(name) {
      if (!QUEUE_NAMES.includes(name)) {
        throw new Error(`Unknown queue: "${name}". Add it to QUEUE_NAMES in src/queues/index.js`);
      }
    
      if (!queues.has(name)) {
        queues.set(name, new Queue(name, { connection: getRedis() }));
      }
    
      return queues.get(name);
    }
    // queues/index.js
    function getAllQueues() {
      QUEUE_NAMES.forEach(getQueue);
      return [...queues.values()]; // ✅ Returns all queue instances
    }
    /**
     * Gracefully closes all open queue connections.
     * Call during process shutdown after workers have been closed.
     */
    async function closeQueues() {
      const closeAll = [...queues.values()].map((q) => q.close().catch(() => {}));
      await Promise.all(closeAll);
      queues.clear();
    }
    
    module.exports = { getQueue, getAllQueues, closeQueues, QUEUE_NAMES };

    +## Chat endpoint
    +
    +`POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/chat` accepts a bearer token and a JSON
    +body containing only a nonempty `message` (up to 8,000 characters):
    +
    +```json
    +{ "message": "Show my workspace dashboard." }
    +```
    +
    +This first HTTP increment returns one complete JSON response using the existing
    +API envelope. For example, after a dashboard read:
    +
    +```json
    +{
    +  "data": {
    +    "text": "Here is your workspace dashboard.",
    +    "modelCalls": 2,
    +    "toolCalls": 2
    +  }
    +}
    +```
    +
    +`modelCalls` and `toolCalls` are server-counted turn metrics; the initial
    +context read is included in `toolCalls`. Successful replies use
    +`Cache-Control: no-store`. Each request starts a fresh conversation. Streaming
    +and server-owned conversation memory remain later increments of the architecture.
    +
    +The route inherits `requireAuth` → `loadDbUser` → `requireMembership` from the
    +workspace router. Context comes exclusively from those middleware results.
    +Client-supplied history, roles, tools, identity fields, model settings, and
    +workspace IDs in the body are rejected. Query parameters cannot change the
    +workspace or actor. The tools offered and executed are still role-filtered
    +Tier 0/1 reads; chat does not execute writes or approve proposals.
    +
    +The dedicated `agentLimiter` allows 10 requests per minute per authenticated
    +user across all workspaces, using the shared Redis store with prefix
    +`rl:agent:`. Existing general limits also apply. A blocked request returns
    +429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` before invoking Groq. As with the existing
    +limiters, initialization failures fall back to an in-memory store with a
    +warning; those fallback counters are local to each process. Request limits and
    +per-completion token caps do not enforce a per-user or workspace spending budget.
    +
    +Validation failures return 400; malformed JSON also returns 400 without echoing
    +the body, and the application's 1 MiB body limit returns 413. Missing/invalid
    +authentication or an unavailable user profile returns 401. An unavailable
    +workspace or membership returns the existing non-enumerating 404. Provider
    +configuration/unavailability/rate limits return 503, timeouts return 504,
    +invalid or truncated completions return 502, and loop/size limits return 422.
    +Errors use the existing `{ error: { code, message, ... } }` API envelope.
    +
    +Provider construction happens per accepted request, so missing Groq settings
    +disable chat with a 503 without preventing the rest of the API from starting.
    +HTTP unit tests run the real application middleware, read loop, and adapter
    +with mocked external services. Throttling tests exercise the memory fallback;
    +shared Redis enforcement and deployed Supabase/Groq behavior still need live
    +integration verification.
    +

    # Agent tools
    
    This module currently provides read tools through `getAvailableTools(context)`
    and `executeReadTool({ name, args, context })`. Server code must build context
    after the existing auth and membership middleware:
    
    ```js
    const context = { userId: req.user.id, member: req.member, workspace: req.workspace };
    ```
    
    `find_member` and `find_container` take `{ query, limit? }`. Queries are trimmed
    and must contain 2–200 characters; limits default to 10 and range from 2 to 20.
    Workspace and actor IDs are always supplied by server context.
    
    Results contain `query`, `status`, `candidates`, and `has_more`. Candidates are
    ranked in PostgreSQL: exact names, literal substrings, then trigram matches,
    with score/name/ID tie-breakers. `score` is a similarity value, not a probability.
    Members must be active and not deleted; containers may be archived/completed
    but must not be deleted. Both searches exclude deleted workspaces.
    
    - `not_found`: no candidates.
    - `single_match`: one candidate to confirm with the user before a write.
    - `ambiguous`: multiple candidates; the user must choose or refine the query.
    
    No result contains an automatically resolved ID. A future proposal executor
    must enforce the user's entity selection separately from action approval.
    `has_more` means further candidates were omitted; refine the query or increase
    the limit. User-supplied names remain untrusted data.
    
    ## Chat endpoint
    
    `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/chat` accepts a bearer token and a JSON
    body containing only a nonempty `message` (up to 8,000 characters):
    
    ```json
    { "message": "Show my workspace dashboard." }
    ```
    
    This first HTTP increment returns one complete JSON response using the existing
    API envelope. For example, after a dashboard read:
    
    ```json
    {
      "data": {
        "text": "Here is your workspace dashboard.",
        "modelCalls": 2,
        "toolCalls": 2
      }
    }
    ```
    
    `modelCalls` and `toolCalls` are server-counted turn metrics; the initial
    context read is included in `toolCalls`. Successful replies use
    `Cache-Control: no-store`. Each request starts a fresh conversation. Streaming
    and server-owned conversation memory remain later increments of the architecture.
    
    The route inherits `requireAuth` → `loadDbUser` → `requireMembership` from the
    workspace router. Context comes exclusively from those middleware results.
    Client-supplied history, roles, tools, identity fields, model settings, and
    workspace IDs in the body are rejected. Query parameters cannot change the
    workspace or actor. The tools offered and executed are still role-filtered
    Tier 0/1 reads; chat does not execute writes or approve proposals.
    
    The dedicated `agentLimiter` allows 10 requests per minute per authenticated
    user across all workspaces, using the shared Redis store with prefix
    `rl:agent:`. Existing general limits also apply. A blocked request returns
    429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` before invoking Groq. As with the existing
    limiters, a missing Redis client or synchronous store-construction failure
    falls back to an in-memory store with a warning; those counters are local to
    each process. Request limits and per-completion token caps do not enforce a
    per-user or workspace spending budget.
    
    Validation failures return 400; malformed JSON also returns 400 without echoing
    the body, and the application's 1 MiB body limit returns 413. Missing/invalid
    authentication or an unavailable user profile returns 401. An unavailable
    workspace or membership returns the existing non-enumerating 404. Provider
    configuration/unavailability/rate limits return 503, timeouts return 504,
    invalid or truncated completions return 502, and loop/size limits return 422.
    Errors use the existing `{ error: { code, message, ... } }` API envelope.
    
    Provider construction happens per accepted request, so missing Groq settings
    disable chat with a 503 without preventing the rest of the API from starting.
    HTTP unit tests run the real application middleware, read loop, and adapter
    with mocked external services. Throttling tests exercise the memory fallback;
    shared Redis enforcement and deployed Supabase/Groq behavior still need live
    integration verification.
    
    ## Internal read loop
    
    `runReadTurn({ data: { message }, context, provider })` in
    `services/read-loop.service.js` runs one fresh read-only turn. Server code
    supplies the authenticated context and the provider. Client data accepts only
    a text message; conversation history, roles, tool results, and workspace IDs
    are rejected. Each invocation starts with `get_my_context` and keeps its
    messages and authenticated identity local to that invocation.
    
    The injected provider implements:
    
    ```js
    provider.chat({ messages, tools })
    // -> { text: string | null, toolCalls: [{ id, name, arguments: string }] }
    ```
    
    Messages use chat-completion roles and correlated `tool_call_id` values.
    Tool definitions contain `name`, `description`, and the Zod `parameterSchema`;
    the provider adapter owns converting schemas to its wire format. Only the
    caller's permitted Tier 0/1 definitions are supplied. Every execution still
    passes through `executeReadTool` and the handler's permission checks.
    
    Tool messages wrap results in `{ kind: 'untrusted_tool_result', data }`, and
    the fixed system instruction treats their contents as data and forbids
    arithmetic. This preserves the instruction/data boundary; live-model prompt
    injection and numerical-fidelity evaluations are still required.
    
    The loop permits at most 6 model calls and 12 tool calls (including context),
    8,000 input characters, 16,000 reply characters, 64 KiB per tool result, and
    128 KiB of conversation messages. It rejects unavailable tools, reused call
    IDs, malformed responses/arguments, and oversized results. Errors terminate
    the turn; transport and unexpected service details are not returned to callers.
    Success returns `{ text, modelCalls, toolCalls }`. Turn and tool traces share
    a server-generated `turnId`; rejected batches identify their requested tools.
    
    Workspace token budgets, streaming, and server-owned conversation memory are
    subsequent increments.
    
    ## Groq adapter
    
    `providers/groq.provider.js` exports `createGroqProvider()`, which implements
    the loop's provider interface using Node's built-in `fetch`:
    
    ```js
    const { createGroqProvider } = require('./providers/groq.provider');
    const { runReadTurn } = require('./services/read-loop.service');
    const provider = createGroqProvider();
    const reply = await runReadTurn({ data: { message }, context, provider });
    ```
    
    Set `GROQ_API_KEY` and `GROQ_MODEL` on the server; both are required. Choose a
    standard model that supports function calling. Compound model IDs are rejected
    because those systems can execute provider-hosted tools outside Kith. Only
    function definitions already selected by the loop are sent to Groq, and
    responses that contain provider-executed or undeclared tools are rejected.
    
    The adapter converts Zod input schemas using `zod-to-json-schema`. This gives
    the model structural constraints; the registry remains responsible for full
    Zod validation, including refinements and transformations. Handler functions,
    server context objects, and credentials are not serialized into tool definitions.
    
    `GROQ_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 20000 (maximum 60000) and covers both the request
    and response-body read. `GROQ_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS` defaults to 1024 (maximum
    4096). Requests and streamed response bodies are capped at 256 KiB. The
    endpoint is fixed to Groq's HTTPS chat-completions API, redirects are rejected,
    and requests are non-streaming with one completion and no automatic retries.
    
    Successful responses normalize to the existing `{ text, toolCalls }` contract.
    Truncated, malformed, or inconsistent completions terminate the turn. Timeout
    and rate-limit codes survive the loop boundary, but upstream messages, bodies,
    reasoning fields, and credentials are not exposed to callers or logs. Provider
    token usage, model, HTTP status, and latency are logged when available; this
    does not yet enforce a per-user or per-workspace spending budget.
    
    Unit tests use synthetic Groq responses, Web Streams, and the real read loop.
    They do not make live model calls or verify a deployed model's behavior.
    Reference: [Groq chat API](https://console.groq.com/docs/api-reference#chat-create)
    and [tool use](https://console.groq.com/docs/tool-use).

    };
    
    const lastSeenKey   = (userId) => `kith:lastseen:${userId}`;
    const membershipKey = (workspaceId, userId) => `kith:membership:${workspaceId}:${userId}`;

    // are deliberately NOT part of this cached payload — see dashboard.service.js.
    // v2 skips payloads cached before target/participant workspace isolation
    // was enforced. Old keys expire normally without being served again.
    const dashboardKey      = (workspaceId, isAdmin) => `kith:dashboard:v2:${workspaceId}:${isAdmin ? 'admin' : 'member'}`;
    const overdueSummaryKey = (workspaceId) => `kith:overdue-summary:v2:${workspaceId}`;
    
    module.exports = { TTL, lastSeenKey, membershipKey, dashboardKey, overdueSummaryKey };

    //

    // Two distinct limiters cover two distinct threat models:
    //
    //   generalLimiter   — mounted globally in app.js, BEFORE any auth

    //

    const rateLimit = require('express-rate-limit');
    // rate-limit-redis v4's CJS export is { RedisStore, default }, not a bare
    // constructor — `require('rate-limit-redis')` alone is not `new`-able.
    const { RedisStore } = require('rate-limit-redis');
    const { getRedis } = require('../config/redis');
    const logger = require('../utils/logger');
    
    function buildStore(prefix) {
      try {
        const redis = getRedis();
        if (!redis || typeof redis.call !== 'function') {
          logger.warn(`Rate limiter [${prefix}]: Redis client unavailable or missing .call() — falling back to in-memory store. Rate limits will NOT be shared across instances.`);
          return undefined;
        }
        return new RedisStore({
          sendCommand: (...args) => redis.call(...args),
          prefix,

> For the agent’s usage budget, should each workspace share one allowance, or should each user have a separate allowance across workspaces? I’ll prepare token accounting while this is decided.

Shared allowance per workspace (Recommended)

    const { z } = require('zod');
    
    const tokenCount = z.number().int().nonnegative().max(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
    const tokenUsageSchema = z.object({
      promptTokens: tokenCount,
      completionTokens: tokenCount,
      totalTokens: tokenCount,
    }).strict().refine((usage) => Number.isSafeInteger(usage.promptTokens + usage.completionTokens)
      && usage.totalTokens === usage.promptTokens + usage.completionTokens, {
      message: 'Token usage must contain consistent totals',
    });
    
    const traceId = z.string().min(1).max(128).regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/);
    // Server metadata only; the adapter must never serialize it into a model request.
    const providerTraceSchema = z.object({
      requestId: traceId.optional(),
      turnId: traceId,
      workspaceId: traceId,
      actorUserId: traceId,
      actorMemberId: traceId,
      modelCall: z.number().int().positive().max(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER),
    }).strict();
    
    module.exports = { tokenCount, tokenUsageSchema, providerTraceSchema };

     a server-generated `turnId`; rejected batches identify their requested tools.
    +Provider calls receive a separate server-owned `trace` with the HTTP request
    +ID (when available), turn ID, workspace/caller IDs, and model-call index. The
    +Groq adapter uses this only for local logs; it is not sent to the model.
     
    +## Token accounting and budget scope
    +
    +The adapter normalizes provider-reported prompt, completion, and total token
    +counts. Counts must be nonnegative safe integers, and the total must equal
    +prompt plus completion tokens. Unknown provider metadata is discarded.
    +Missing usage remains `null`, not a claim of zero consumption.
    +
    +Usage is parsed before completion validation. A truncated or rejected
    +completion can therefore retain valid usage on its canonical error's internal
    +`usage` property. Normalization preserves only validated counts; that property
    +is separate from client-facing error details and is not serialized into HTTP
    +errors. Unreadable bodies, timeouts without usage, and invalid usage remain
    +unreported. Successful HTTP responses also keep their existing shape.
    +
    +Each turn's success or failure trace contains a `usage` summary:
    +`knownPromptTokens`, `knownCompletionTokens`, `knownTotalTokens`,
    +`reportedModelCalls`, `unreportedModelCalls`, and `complete`. Totals include
    +reported usage from failed completions and calls followed by tool failures.
    +`complete` describes accounting coverage, not whether the turn succeeded.
    +When usage is incomplete, the known totals are only a partial count. The loop
    +rejects aggregate totals that cannot be represented safely instead of rounding.
    +
    +These are per-turn structured logs and internal provider metadata, not a
    +durable quota ledger. The agreed budget scope is **one shared allowance per
    +workspace**. The allowance amount, reset schedule, reservation/reconciliation
    +policy, and durable enforcement remain for the budget milestone.

    if (REDIS_URL) {
      try {

        const url = new URL(REDIS_URL);
        redisHostname = url.hostname;
        useTLS = url.protocol === 'rediss:'; // only TLS if scheme says so
      } catch (e) {
        logger.error('Failed to parse REDIS_URL', { error: e.message });
      }
    }

      enableReadyCheck: false,

      ...(useTLS && {
        tls: {

          rejectUnauthorized: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',

      retryStrategy(times) {
        const delay = Math.min(times * 100, 3000);
        return delay;
      },
    };
    
    let redis;
    
    function getRedis() {
      if (!redis) {
        // Check if REDIS_URL exists
        if (!process.env.REDIS_URL) {

          throw new Error('REDIS_URL is required');
        }
    
        logger.info('Connecting to Redis', {
          host: redisHostname,
          tlsEnabled: useTLS
        });
    
        redis = new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL, redisOptions);
    
        redis.on('error', (err) => {
          logger.error('Redis error', { error: err.message, stack: err.stack });
        });
    
        redis.on('connect', () => {
          logger.info('Redis connected successfully');
        });
    
        redis.on('ready', () => {
          logger.info('Redis ready');

        redis.on('close', () => {
          logger.warn('Redis connection closed');
        });
    
        redis.on('reconnecting', () => {
          logger.warn('Redis reconnecting...');
        });

    // One hash per workspace/window. All changes are atomic within Redis.
    // Pending reservations remain charged until a known outcome replaces them.
    const RESERVE_SCRIPT = `
    local function integer(n) return n and n >= 0 and n <= 9007199254740991.0 and n == math.floor(n) end
    local function text(n) return string.format('%.0f', n) end
    local clock = redis.call('TIME')
    local now = tonumber(clock[1]) * 1000.0 + math.floor(tonumber(clock[2]) / 1000.0)
    local start_at = tonumber(ARGV[1])
    local reset_at = tonumber(ARGV[2])
    local requested_limit = tonumber(ARGV[3])
    local amount = tonumber(ARGV[4])
    local field = 'r:' .. ARGV[5]
    local expires_at = tonumber(ARGV[6])
    if now < start_at or now >= reset_at then return {'stale', text(now)} end
    
    local raw = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], 'used', 'limit', 'blocked')
    local used = raw[1] and tonumber(raw[1]) or 0
    local limit = raw[2] and tonumber(raw[2]) or requested_limit
    if not integer(used) or not integer(limit) or limit < 1 then return {'invalid'} end
    if raw[3] and raw[3] ~= '1' then return {'invalid'} end
    if (raw[1] and not raw[2]) or (raw[2] and not raw[1]) then return {'invalid'} end
    -- A rolling deployment cannot raise the active window's stored allowance.
    limit = math.min(limit, requested_limit)
    redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'used', text(used), 'limit', text(limit))
    redis.call('PEXPIREAT', KEYS[1], expires_at)
    if raw[3] then return {'blocked'} end
    
    local previous = redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], field)
    if previous then
      local pending = tonumber(string.match(previous, '^p:(%d+)$'))
      if pending then
        if pending ~= amount then return {'invalid'} end
        return {'reserved', text(used), text(limit)}
      end
      if string.match(previous, '^s:%d+$') then return {'settled'} end
      return {'invalid'}
    end
    if amount > limit then return {'too_large'} end
    if used >= limit or used + amount > limit then return {'exhausted'} end
    redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'used', text(used + amount), field, 'p:' .. text(amount))
    return {'reserved', text(used + amount), text(limit)}
    `;
    
    const SETTLE_SCRIPT = `
    local function integer(n) return n and n >= 0 and n <= 9007199254740991.0 and n == math.floor(n) end
    local function text(n) return string.format('%.0f', n) end
    local field = 'r:' .. ARGV[1]
    local previous = redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], field)
    if not previous then return {'missing'} end
    local used = tonumber(redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], 'used'))
    if not integer(used) then return {'invalid'} end
    local settled = tonumber(string.match(previous, '^s:(%d+)$'))
    if settled then
      if not integer(settled) then return {'invalid'} end
      return {'settled', text(used), text(settled)}
    end
    local pending = tonumber(string.match(previous, '^p:(%d+)$'))
    if not integer(pending) or used < pending then return {'invalid'} end
    -- Unknown usage keeps its reservation; later known usage may reconcile it.
    if ARGV[2] == '' then return {'held', text(used), text(pending)} end
    local actual = tonumber(ARGV[2])
    if not integer(actual) then return {'invalid'} end
    local next_used = used - pending + actual
    if not integer(next_used) then
      redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'blocked', '1')
      return {'blocked'}
    end
    redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'used', text(next_used), field, 's:' .. text(actual))
    return {'settled', text(next_used), text(actual)}
    `;
    
    module.exports = { RESERVE_SCRIPT, SETTLE_SCRIPT };

    const { randomUUID } = require('crypto');
    const { z } = require('zod');
    const { getRedis } = require('../../config/redis');
    const { TTL, agentBudgetKey } = require('../../config/redis-keys');
    const { ForbiddenError, ValidationError } = require('../../utils/errors');
    const logger = require('../../utils/logger');
    const { assertAgentContext } = require('./context.service');
    const { providerError } = require('../providers/provider-errors');
    const { tokenUsageSchema } = require('../validators/provider-metadata.validator');
    const { budgetConfigSchema, reservationSchema, reserveReplySchema, settleReplySchema } = require('../validators/budget.validator');
    const { RESERVE_SCRIPT, SETTLE_SCRIPT } = require('./budget-scripts');
    
    function budgetWindow(period, timestamp) {
      const date = new Date(timestamp);
      if (!Number.isSafeInteger(timestamp) || Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
        throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
      }
      const year = date.getUTCFullYear();
      const month = date.getUTCMonth();
      const day = period === 'day' ? date.getUTCDate() : 1;
      return {
        windowStartMs: Date.UTC(year, month, day),
        resetAtMs: period === 'day' ? Date.UTC(year, month, day + 1) : Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 1),
      };
    }
    
    /** Workspace identity is captured from authenticated middleware, never model data. */
    function createWorkspaceBudget({ context, limit, period, timeoutMs = 3000, redisFactory = getRedis, now = Date.now } = {}) {
      assertAgentContext(context);
      if (!z.string().uuid().safeParse(context.workspace.id).success) throw new ForbiddenError('Active workspace membership required');
      const parsed = budgetConfigSchema.safeParse({ limit, period, timeoutMs });
      if (!parsed.success || typeof redisFactory !== 'function' || typeof now !== 'function') {
        throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_CONFIGURATION');
      }
      const config = parsed.data;
      const workspaceId = context.workspace.id.toLowerCase();
      const actorUserId = context.userId;
    
      async function command(script, key, args) {
        let timer;
        try {
          const redis = redisFactory();
          // The shared BullMQ client retries indefinitely. Budget checks have their
          // own deadline and require a ready connection; there is no local fallback.
          if (redis?.status !== 'ready' || typeof redis.eval !== 'function') throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
          const deadline = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
            timer = setTimeout(() => reject(providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE')), config.timeoutMs);
          });
          return await Promise.race([redis.eval(script, 1, key, ...args), deadline]);
        } catch {
          logger.warn('Agent token budget command failed', { workspaceId, actorUserId });
          throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
        } finally {
          clearTimeout(timer);
        }
      }
    
      return Object.freeze({
        async reserve({ tokens } = {}) {
          if (!Number.isSafeInteger(tokens) || tokens < 0 || tokens > 1000000000) throw new ValidationError('Invalid agent token reservation');
          const id = randomUUID();
          let window = budgetWindow(config.period, now());
          // Redis time detects clock skew or a reset while the command was queued.
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt += 1) {
            const key = agentBudgetKey(workspaceId, config.period, window.windowStartMs);
            const raw = await command(RESERVE_SCRIPT, key, [
              window.windowStartMs, window.resetAtMs, config.limit, tokens, id,
              window.resetAtMs + TTL.AGENT_BUDGET_RETENTION_SECONDS * 1000,
            ]);
            const parsedReply = reserveReplySchema.safeParse(raw);
            if (!parsedReply.success) throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
            const [state, value] = parsedReply.data;
            if (state === 'stale') {
              window = budgetWindow(config.period, value);
              continue;
            }
            if (state === 'reserved') {
              return Object.freeze({ id, workspaceId, period: config.period, ...window, reservedTokens: tokens });
            }
            if (state === 'too_large') throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE');
            if (state === 'exhausted' || state === 'blocked') {
              logger.info('Agent workspace token allowance exhausted', { workspaceId, actorUserId, resetAtMs: window.resetAtMs });
              throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED', undefined, window.resetAtMs);
            }
            throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
          }
          throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
        },
    
        async settle({ reservation, usage = null } = {}) {
          const parsedReservation = reservationSchema.safeParse(reservation);
          if (!parsedReservation.success) throw new ValidationError('Invalid agent token reservation');
          const ticket = parsedReservation.data;
          if (ticket.workspaceId !== workspaceId) throw new ForbiddenError('The reservation belongs to another workspace');
          const expectedWindow = budgetWindow(ticket.period, ticket.windowStartMs);
          if (ticket.windowStartMs !== expectedWindow.windowStartMs || ticket.resetAtMs !== expectedWindow.resetAtMs) {
            throw new ValidationError('Invalid agent budget window');
          }
          const parsedUsage = tokenUsageSchema.nullable().safeParse(usage);
          if (!parsedUsage.success) throw new ValidationError('Invalid agent token usage');
          const key = agentBudgetKey(workspaceId, ticket.period, ticket.windowStartMs);
          const raw = await command(SETTLE_SCRIPT, key, [ticket.id, parsedUsage.data ? String(parsedUsage.data.totalTokens) : '']);
          const parsedReply = settleReplySchema.safeParse(raw);
          if (!parsedReply.success || !['settled', 'held'].includes(parsedReply.data[0])) throw providerError('AGENT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE');
          const [state, usedTokens, chargedTokens] = parsedReply.data;
          logger.info('Agent token reservation reconciled', { workspaceId, actorUserId, reservationId: ticket.id, state, usedTokens, chargedTokens });
          return { state, usedTokens, chargedTokens };
        },
      });
    }
    
    module.exports = { createWorkspaceBudget };
